questions.prompt: You have the nut flush on the river against one opponent who calls too much. Best default?

choices.text: Check so you can trap a raise that will not come

questions.explanation: The nuts want a big call from worse flushes, sets, and stubborn one-pair hands.

questions.prompt: You have top pair, decent kicker, on a dry river against a calling station. A small value bet…

choices.text: Can be right. They call with worse pairs.
Must be a check because top pair is weak

questions.explanation: Stations pay thin value. Do not turn the bet into a size only the nuts can call.

questions.prompt: Same top pair against a tight player who folds one pair. Best default?

choices.text: Check. A bet gets called by better and folds out worse.

questions.explanation: If they only continue when they beat you, the bet is not value.

questions.prompt: You bet the river for value and face a raise. With one pair you…

choices.text: Fold most of the time. River raises are strong, especially live.
Call because the bet was for value

questions.explanation: Live river raises are value-heavy. One pair is a bluff-catcher at best, and usually a fold to the raise.
